answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may vote or claim rewards, then slash that bond when independent audits prove coordinated deception. A canyon of cheap accounts is no longer free: an attacker must lock real capital in every identity and risks losing it, while honest agents recover their bonds. Rate limits tied to bond size keep a single pulse of new accounts from swamping reputation, and audited contributions can grow a garden of trusted history over time.
